TS09 — Cross-dataset and cross-asset forecasting audit¶

Goal¶

Test a fixed representative model menu across six stock histories and two public climate series, retaining equal-priority smoothed-level and actual-change tracks. Separate per-dataset chronological selection from aggregate evaluation, preserve correlated panel structure in resampling, and audit what “independent” can mean. This is a historical generalization study, not an untouched or prospective test.

Observed results¶

Six stocks were evaluated on 64 common scored origins per horizon, plus two monthly physical datasets. Equal-asset five-session returns MSE skill is -0.0984, with 1/6 positive asset scores. Equal-asset five-session smoothed MSE skill is -0.0871, with 2/6 positive asset scores. Per-asset, monthly-dataset, block and synchronized-uncertainty results are reported separately. Historical inputs were previously examined; independence and prospective validation remain unestablished.

Setup¶

Use the existing statsmodels/scikit-learn/CPU PyTorch environment. Inputs, source metadata, protocol and previous notebooks are bundled; no download or prior notebook execution is required. TS09_PROTOCOL.json was frozen before benchmark execution. It declares the universe, transforms, budgets, schedules, candidate menu and aggregation. The complete package is maintained under one stable name for subsequent updates.

Steps¶

1. Inspect provenance, units and exposure before computing scores¶

Stock inputs use the common observed session index from 2021-01-04 through 2026-10-01: 1,443 rows per asset. The first five caches explicitly adjusted OHLC by provider Adj Close / Close; the NVDA cache used auto_adjust=True. The producer's adjustment code and cache byte hashes are preserved. These histories were examined elsewhere in the project. Adjusted prices are not executable quotes or a point-in- time corporate-action database; use no pristine test label.

El Niño uses all 732 monthly NOAA temperature observations in the statsmodels bundle (1950–2010), in Celsius levels, not logarithms of Celsius. CO2 uses monthly means of finite weekly measurements from 1965 onward, in ppm levels; all 444 months have at least one measurement. No interpolation or future filling is performed. Monthly stamps represent period-end observational availability by convention; actual historical publication delays and vintages are unavailable. These climate examples are retrospective signal benchmarks, not operational release- time forecasts. Stock horizons are at most five sessions; climate horizons are at most five monthly observations.

The legacy track key returns denotes actual future signal change. For stocks it is cumulative log return; for climate it is a Celsius or ppm difference. The smoothed key denotes future causal EMA signal level. Do not pool raw physical-unit errors or call a temperature difference an investment return.

2. Freeze representative models and nested schedules¶

All datasets use causal EMA rates 0.2/0.05 and the previous supervised 20 × 2 input. Ridge(alpha=10), fixed histogram boosting, GRU and NBEATS_demo learn five outputs from smoothed changes only. AR(5) forecasts smoothed changes natively and uses the previous restricted OLS bridge to actual signal changes. Thus this is a comparison of complete procedures, not an isolated architecture experiment.

Neural models retain three fixed seeds, width 12, at most 30 epochs, patience 5, purged 20% chronological stopping, then same-seed reset/refit on mature examples. Their predictions are equally averaged; any failed member triggers a whole-family null fallback. At most 252 mature examples are used. The smaller/earlier climate fits can have fewer examples; their counts are exported. Parameters are fitted separately on each dataset; this is not a model trained on SPY and transferred without fitting to another asset.

Climate also includes a period-12 seasonal benchmark: repeat the last observed 12 fast-EMA differences and invert the EMA recursion for future actual changes. This is not a raw-level seasonal-naive forecast. It receives no future observation. Nulls are always eligible; drift and slope benchmarks are reported but not selected.

Before each outer block, select separately by dataset and track using equal-horizon relative MAE at earlier inner origins whose full five-label vectors have matured. Freeze the choice within that block, while refitting model parameters at each origin. Stocks: starts 800/1000/1200, six inner origins 20 sessions apart, outer step 10. El Niño: starts 450/540/630, four inner origins 10 months apart, outer step 10. CO2: starts 320/360/400, four inner origins 10 months apart, outer step 5. Only complete five-horizon outer cohorts are scored; latest queries stay unscored. The delivered model stage is cached with exact protocol, source, output and checkpoint hashes. Reruns reuse it only when all hashes match; set RECOMPUTE=True below to refit every model. This separates expensive fitting from repeatable chart inspection.

        'seeds':tuple(protocol['schedules'][key]['seeds'])})
    schedules.append({'dataset_id':identifier,**asdict(spec)})

3. Compare each dataset before summarizing¶

MSE skill is $1-MSE_{model}/MSE_{null}$ on identical origins and targets within a dataset. Positive is better. The null is filter-aware unchanged-price propagation for the smoothed level and zero change for actual change. Smoothed persistence is not the principal null. A fixed-family score averages that family's three seeds at every origin; selected_pipeline is the procedure chosen only from past inner data. A high family score discovered afterward cannot replace the selected history.

Report results by dataset, horizon and predeclared outer block. Stock targets and source vintages differ from earlier notebooks' snapshots/cohorts; do not infer a performance change merely by comparing these numbers with TS07 or TS08 summaries.

models=['selected_pipeline','AR5_changes','Ridge_10','HistBoost','GRU','NBEATS_demo']
fig,axes=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,5))
for ax,track in zip(axes,['smoothed','returns']):
    table=scores[(scores.dataset_id.isin(stock_ids))&(scores.track==track)&(scores.horizon==5)&(scores.model.isin(models))].pivot(index='dataset_id',columns='model',values='MSE_skill').reindex(index=stock_ids,columns=models)
    image=ax.imshow(table.to_numpy(),cmap='RdYlGn',vmin=-.5,vmax=.5,aspect='auto')
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(models)),['Selected','AR5','Ridge','Boost','GRU','NBEATS'],rotation=35,ha='right')
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(stock_ids)),stock_ids);ax.set_title(f'{track.title()} — five-session MSE skill')
    for i in range(len(table)):
        for j in range(len(models)):ax.text(j,i,f'{table.iloc[i,j]:.2f}',ha='center',va='center',fontsize=8)
    ax.grid(False)
    fig.colorbar(image,ax=ax,label='MSE skill (clipped ±0.5)',fraction=.04,pad=.04)
save_figure(fig,OUT,'02_stock_model_comparison');

4. Keep domain aggregation explicit and inspect monthly seasonality¶

Average within-dataset skill with equal dataset weights; never pool squared Celsius, ppm and log-price errors. Stocks and nonfinancial datasets have separate aggregates. The stock basket is a convenience universe from prior work, not a random sample of assets: it overrepresents related technology names. Six assets on the same 64 dates are not six independent replications. Some positive/negative dataset counts may summarize this basket but do not estimate market-wide success rates.

The monthly examples use the same causal smoothed-feature representation, with an extra seasonal candidate suited to their sampling frequency. A five-month result is a general library demonstration, not a five-day trading forecast.

5. Preserve cross-asset dependence in historical uncertainty¶

Per-dataset moving-block ranges compare selected-minus-null absolute loss at horizon five. Blocks count scheduled origins, not days/months. The synchronized stock-panel calculation first divides each asset's loss difference by that asset's full-cohort null MAE, then averages assets equally. The same time blocks are sampled across all six assets, preserving contemporaneous dependence.

The null denominators remain fixed during this conditional resampling. Ranges are not MSE-skill confidence intervals, a bootstrap of independent assets or corrections for prior exploration/model searches. Negative differences favor selection. Treat block lengths 1/2/4 as sensitivity choices, not a search for a favorable interval.

Checks — information timing is necessary, not sufficient for independent evidence¶

The audit distinguishes computational timing from research independence. Correct prefixes and nested selection prevent specific leakage mechanisms, but cannot erase prior inspection, convenience-universe selection or revised historical inputs. No result here is labeled paper_validated, and no outer winner replaces a frozen past choice. A prospective specification is bundled; it has not been started or scheduled and has no collected outcomes.

for name in ['tabular_audit','neural_audit']:
    a=combined[name];assert (a.max_training_label<=a.origin_pos).all()
a=combined['classical_audit'];assert (a.bridge_last_label_pos<=a.origin_pos).all()

(OUT/'run_manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest,indent=2))
summary='## Observed results'+chr(10)*2+'Six stocks were evaluated on **64 common scored origins** per horizon, plus two monthly physical datasets. '
for row in macro.query('group=="stocks" and model=="selected_pipeline" and horizon==5').itertuples():
    summary+=f'Equal-asset five-session **{row.track}** MSE skill is **{row.mean_MSE_skill:.4f}**, with **{row.positive_datasets}/6** positive asset scores. '
summary+='Per-asset, monthly-dataset, block and synchronized-uncertainty results are reported separately. Historical inputs were previously examined; independence and prospective validation remain unestablished.'
(OUT/'observed_summary.md').write_text(summary)
print('PASS: frozen protocol, mature inner/training labels, matched cohorts and honest independence audit.')

Next Steps¶

TS10 can connect the forecasting library to NB9/NB10 only after explicitly mapping same-origin targets to executable entry/exit timing. TS09 does not authorize live trades or imply that historical skill survives transaction costs. The bundled prospective plan starts no earlier than 2026-11-02 and requires newly issued forecasts and data-vintage hashes stored before outcomes; it is a specification, not an active collection service or a completed acceptance test.

Primary references: Time-series cross-validation, statsmodels El Niño data, statsmodels CO2 data. Public teaching data and revised stock caches have different provenance limits; separate their evidence from a future prospective paper-forecast record.
